title: PI plan — tranche 11 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
body:
# PI plan — tranche 11 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Objectives

- **O1 — S14 is accepted on its surviving evidence and stays active.** The cutover project's charter, seven A–D artefacts, scope baseline, delivery contract and Phase-G review are placed, and its receipt is green. Issue #29 remains open, so the project does not close and no closure is claimed.
- **O2 — T6 is re-closed through its closure gate.** The development-project record is reworked to the v4 standard and closed with a compliant Phase-G review and a published retrospective closure review.
- **O3 — T8 is re-closed through its closure gate.** The organisational-memory record is reworked to the v4 standard and closed with a compliant Phase-G review and a published retrospective closure review.
- **O4 — the tranche-11 SAFe gaps clear.** The four cadence rows and this plan's metadata discharge `pi_cadence_missing:tranche-11` and `backlog_refinement_missing:tranche-11`, and the exit gate hands #755 three fresh receipts.

## Plan

The three members are reworked by the retrospective factory against the same replay record, one pack each, in the order the tranche's refinement records. Readiness (four cadences, the two PI documents, the plan approval and the retro lesson) is written first because two tranche-scope P1 packages are due the moment the tranche is authorised, and every member's `pi_cadence`, `pi_plan`, `pi_objectives` and `lessons` checks read it.

T6 and T8 are closed projects whose manifests pinned them `active`; this tranche re-pins each to the close its record already carries, and each pack supplies the closure content the factory refuses to close without. S14 is active and stays active: its only open unit is #29, the cutover plan rewrite, and `--keep-active` is the computed route.

The execution order is WSJF order: T8, then S14, then T6. The factory's own roster is sorted by project key (S14, T6, T8) and is not rewritten to match: the two orders answer different questions, and the refinement is the re-estimate of record.

## WSJF order

| rank | member | business value | time criticality | risk reduction | job size | WSJF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T8 | 8 | 5 | 7 | 5 | 4.00 |
| 2 | S14 | 8 | 7 | 9 | 8 | 3.00 |
| 3 | T6 | 9 | 6 | 8 | 8 | 2.875 |

T8 ranks first because it is the smallest job and its capability — two independent evidence refs and a human review before a lesson becomes doctrine — is what every later lesson in the programme runs on. S14 ranks second because its cutover carries the largest risk reduction: a rollback that has not been rehearsed is the programme's largest single failure mode. T6 ranks third because it is the largest job and depends on T5 and T13, both already delivered.

## Capacity and WIP

- One live record writer: the replay record is shared with the tranche-10 (#964) and tranche-12 (#961) lanes, so the tranche-11 rows are written by one session at a time and only at `period='tranche-11'`.
- One factory invocation: `rework-batch.py` is serial and refuses a dirty lane; the tranche-11 journal (`docs/evidence/rework/batch/tranche-11.jsonl`) is its single lock.
- WIP limits: two open batches and one open card per writer. T8 is cleared first so its close is not competing with a second member's cards.
- Read agents: at most six, and no second full test suite on this box while a record write is in flight.

## Evidence

The packs are preflighted by `scripts/rework-content-check.py` at one pinned snapshot, each with its refinement WSJF and its computed `--closes` (false for S14, true for T6 and T8). The receipts are rendered by `scripts/verify-project.py` and the exit by `scripts/check-tranche-exit.py`; the readiness gate records the snapshot path, its manifest sha256 and the three checker results. The register this work answers is `docs/evidence/rework-register.json`; the tranche's two tranche-scope packages and the members' missing v4 categories are enumerated in `docs/evidence/rework/tranche-11/readiness-gate.md`.

## Dependencies

- **#755** — the tranche-10 review is the only writer of tranche 11's authorisation; the dry run and every receipt wait for it.
- **#964** — tranche 10's preparation lane; the review chain's immediate predecessor.
- **#961** — tranche 12's preparation lane, in flight in parallel; it shares the replay record and no tranche-11 file.
- **#852** — the promotion. This lane writes the replay record only; nothing here reaches production.

## Backlog refinement

The refinement re-estimates each member by its measured v4 gap rather than its open-package count, because the standard's `scope.through_tranche: 8` marks tranche-11 artefact packages `scheduled` and the package list reads almost empty (two tranche-scope packages, zero per member) while the register's `missing` list carries 16 categories for S14, 13 for T6 and 15 for T8. It reorders the seed's membership (S14, T6, T8) to T8, S14, T6 for the reasons in the WSJF order, and records the four integers of each member as the PI's re-estimate of record.

The two tranche-scope packages `pi_cadence_missing:tranche-11` and `backlog_refinement_missing:tranche-11` are the refinement's own discharge: they clear when these rows and this record exist, and they are the reason the readiness step precedes every pack.
